To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the thyroid glands of rats which had received 26,400 rds of 131I radiation and had been stimulated with thiouracil 2 or 8 months after radiation, displayed an unusual pattern of DNA synthesis in individual cells.

thyroid cells of rats, exposed to 2640 rads of 131I and subsequently stimulated by thiouracil, display some transient impairment in DNA synthesis, but at 2 months, DNA synthesis and thyroidal weight increase to levels greater than in nonradiated controls.
thyroid cells of rats exposed to a high dose of 13I radiation, and then stimulated to increase synthesis of DNA and growth, showed unusual changes in the amount of nuclear DNA and nuclear volume.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of radiation on thyroid function, with the hope that a more complete knowledge of the effects on the cell may be useful in clinical management of patients with hyperthyroidism and cancer of the thyroid.
the effects of radiation on thyroid cells.
the effect of radiation on thyroid function and structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
131I radiation in doses sufficient to produce a 50% decrease in thyroidal weight in rats does not cause a permanent decrease in the capacity of the gland for DNA synthesis.
the thyroid is a target for 131I and that the effects of 131I on the gland are complex.
the DNA synthesis in the thyroid gland of rats after irradiation with 131I, as measured in this investigation, was not impaired.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of 131I on the thyroid gland are not limited to obvious destruction of cells, but also involve subtle damage to the DNA of the cells which remain.
the thyroid is a very radiosensitive gland and the thyroid cells are very radiosensitive cells.
the thyroid gland is capable of considerable regeneration, but that the regenerative capacity of this organ is not infinite.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use a single cell to measure the effects of radiation on DNA synthesis in a single cell.
the thyroid gland is very resilient.
the radiation dose is not the most important factor in determining the severity of thyroid dysfunction after 131I treatment of Graves' disease, as has previously been thought.
